```plato

    //==
    // # Discretizing curves and surfaces
    //
    // Evaluating a curve, a polar curve, or a parametric surface at evenly spaced
    // parameters, and turning the samples into polylines. Split out of the curve
    // interface bodies because discretization is a single concern with a single
    // convention (open curves include both endpoints, closed ones omit the duplicate
    // seam) and because it is the one part of the curve package that reaches into
    // the P2 collection primitives.

    //==
    // # Sampling and discretization
    //
    // Evaluating a curve or surface at evenly spaced parameters. The
    // discretization primitives are `Fractions` (endpoints included, the right
    // form for an OPEN curve) and `FractionsExclusive` (upper end omitted, the
    // right form for a CLOSED one), both in
    // `collections.library.plato` (P2). P6 may call P2.
    //
    // A closed curve satisfies Eval(0) = Eval(1), so sampling it with
    // `Fractions` would duplicate the seam point; the periodic samplers below
    // use `FractionsExclusive` and hand `Closed = true` to the polyline, which
    // re-joins the ends itself.

    // `count` values evenly spaced over the canonical domain, endpoints
    // included. One body for every embedding, via the generic `ICurve<TRange>`
    // root: sampling needs `Eval` and nothing else. Precondition: count >= 2.
    Sample(self: ICurve<$TRange>, count: Integer): Array<$TRange>
        => count.Fractions.Map(t => self.Eval(t));
```
